claim_ceiling: Literature synthesis confirms that aggregation recipe choice ambiguity is a documented measurement phenomenon in at least one strong econometric source (OECD 2008 Handbook composite indicators: arithmetic vs geometric vs weighted product) and one strong psychometric source (Kane & Case mixed-format composite weighting), with a principled MIXED-outcome handling method (OECD/COINr sensitivity analysis/robustness bounds). After correcting duplicate provenance URLs and screened-count inconsistency, the minimum justified counts are M1>=2, M2>=3 distinct, M4>=1 strong method. The mapping from these fields to SPIDER's density metric recipes (per-iteration ≈ micro, per-task ≈ macro) and the claim that psychometrics/econometrics/meta-analysis 'strengthen' or 'provide alternative resolution beyond IR' remain interpretive analogies, not established results, exactly as bounded in the previous audit (EXP-INTEL-35280397316 audit V2/V6). No systematic PubMed/EconLit/Cochrane search was executed as preregistered; the reported search was a non-systematic web synthesis via generic APIs with long-phrase queries. Therefore producer SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST (all four decision-rule conditions met) is not justified at the stated systematic-review ceiling. Maximum justified ceiling: non-systematic synthesis provides additional theoretical grounding (one sensitivity framework) for recipe-choice materiality but does not support systematic-review completeness, does not resolve the MIXED decision-rule amendment, and does not promote C-MEAS-VALID. C-MEAS-VALID remains EXPERIMENTAL pending full-DOM empirical re-run.
